base: Use case: stylized-concept. Create an isolated CHARACTER KEY-POSE SHEET for AlgoLand, not a scene. Input image 1 is the approved canonical boss reference ONLY: copy the wooden monster identity, never the hero or background. CERNE PARTIDO: squat split tree-stump torso, jagged broken crown with visible concentric wood rings, small glowing eyes under wooden brow, compact AMBER HEART in a vertical chest fissure, TWO long articulated timber arms with elbow joints and claw hands, FOUR articulated root legs, restricted moss. Preserve precisely the same anatomy, bark plates, size and proportions in every cell. Elevated three-quarter TOP-DOWN orthographic RPG camera as in the reference, crisp sophisticated pixel-art clusters, warm wood browns, selective outlines. No photorealism, no blur, no dripping sap, no flames, no leafy canopy. Transparent alpha background, NO environment, NO floor tiles, NO rocks, NO hero, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO arrows, NO captions, NO borders. ONE sheet, exactly FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, EIGHT EQUAL cells on an approximately 2048x1024 canvas. Each cell reserves 512x512; full body stays inside its own cell with generous margin even when arms extend. Keep a uniform physical scale for the torso in all poses, same camera, central ground pivot and ground baseline in every cell; do not independently fit each bounding box. NO cropping or limbs crossing between cells. Each cell depicts exactly ONE complete monster. Use small transparent contact shadow only. Key poses must visibly articulate shoulders, elbows, hips and root legs, not merely rotate a rigid sprite.

folhas.prompt: SHEET 01: a continuous TWO-SWEEP COMBO seen facing diagonally DOWN toward the viewer, same facing throughout. Read in row order. TOP ROW four successive keys of sweep A with the monster's RIGHT arm: (1) anticipation, right elbow bent and right claw pulled far back, torso coils, front root feet planted; (2) acceleration, hips and shoulders rotate, bent elbow starts to extend; (3) impact, right claw crosses in front of the lower chest toward the opposite side, maximum extension and powerful low horizontal sweep, left arm balancing; (4) follow-through, right arm reaches its far opposite side and torso visibly rotated. BOTTOM ROW keys of the return sweep B with LEFT arm: (5) left shoulder coils for reverse strike while right arm recovers; (6) left elbow and hips accelerate the reverse horizontal arc; (7) left claw extends through the opposite impact position; (8) both arms return to recognizable balanced ready stance. Important: eight distinct successive mechanically readable poses, SAME character and view, no duplicated generic raised-hand gestures. Keep arms and core visible in each key. No special effects hiding hands.

SHEET 02: VIEWS AND LOCOMOTION, eight poses. Image 2 is the accepted combo sheet for exact character identity and drawing style ONLY; do NOT copy its attack poses. TOP ROW: (1) balanced idle facing DOWN toward viewer, both arms relaxed and four root legs supporting torso; (2) true RIGHT-side profile idle facing right, arms and root legs naturally overlapping in depth; (3) TRUE BACK view facing UP away, show the BACK of the stump, back bark plates and rear roots, NO front eyes, NO glowing chest opening visible through its back, crown still same shape and visible wood rings; (4) LEFT-side profile idle facing left, same anatomy. BOTTOM ROW: four successive keys of a heavy QUADRUPED root-leg walk facing DOWN toward viewer, on the spot, body same size and ground pivot fixed. (5) front-right and rear-left diagonal feet advance while opposite feet support; (6) those diagonal feet plant and absorb weight, torso dips slightly; (7) front-left and rear-right advance while opposite feet now support; (8) opposite diagonal feet plant and torso returns toward idle height. The two halves MUST swap which feet advance; do not redraw one unchanged stance four times. Long arms counterbalance with subtle alternate swings, NOT attack windups. All four legs originate under the same torso, do not turn this creature into a biped. Clear full-body silhouettes. Identical scale across directions and walk keys.

SHEET 03: TWO SPECIAL ATTACKS. Image 2 is the approved combo identity/style reference only. All eight poses face diagonally DOWN toward viewer, same body proportions and root anatomy. TOP ROW four successive keys of ROOT-LEG CHARGE: (1) crouch low, torso leans forward, rear roots compressed and front roots lifted slightly, both elbows tucked back to clearly telegraph charge; (2) rear roots PUSH OFF and extend powerfully, front roots reaching forward, body pitched forward; (3) full forward surge, trunk lowered like a battering ram, both claws trailing at sides, distinct stretched stride; (4) braking, front root feet splay and plant ahead, shoulders recoil and rear legs gather under body. Keep ground registration on the same pivot, movement shown by pose not by sliding whole character across cell. BOTTOM ROW four keys of ROOT CONJURATION: (5) upright, both arms spread outward low, amber heart begins brighter pulse; (6) both claw hands press toward ground and THREE THICK FLEXIBLE ANCHOR ROOTS extend from the underside into the implied ground around him, these are anatomical appendages attached to boss not detached trees; (7) anchored crouch, shoulders brace, chest heart flares intensely amber and short branching energy follows the three roots, peak cast, NO fire or lava; (8) anchor roots visibly withdraw, claw hands lift, core dims to normal and torso returns toward ready. Small root tips and sparse wood splinters allowed near feet, no dirt floor patch, no scenery. Distinguish this stationary rooting cast from the mobile charge with clear gestures. No giant glow obscuring anatomy.

SHEET 04: HEAVY DOUBLE-HAND SLAM AND PHASE-TWO TRANSFORMATION. Image 2 is the accepted model/style reference only. Same boss faces diagonally DOWN in every cell. TOP ROW successive slam poses: (1) both heavy timber arms lifted high ABOVE the jagged crown, elbows flexed and claws pointing inward, hind root feet brace; (2) torso compresses and BOTH shoulders drive forearms downward together, knees/root joints bend, maintain same trunk volume; (3) peak IMPACT, both claw fists pressed firmly at ground level IN FRONT of torso, elbows bent to absorb impact, whole body crouched low and crown lowered, core still visible above hands, sparse wood chips and a narrow amber ground-contact crack only, NO floor patch or scenery; (4) slow recovery, both arms lifting away from ground, torso rises with effort, hands relax. BOTTOM ROW successive phase-two transition: (5) normal stance, chest bark fissure starts opening, small amber cracks between existing chest plates; (6) those SAME chest plates hinge outward, exposing more of the SAME heart, shoulders tense and root feet spread; (7) full exposed amber heart within a clearly WIDER chest cavity, jagged bark plates pushed aside but attached, intense compact amber glow contained in the body, head/crown/arms/legs remain SAME dimensions, not a new monster; (8) enraged combat-ready stance, chest remains exposed, trunk leans forward, one claw forward and one cocked back ready to attack. Do NOT add armor, horns, fire, wings or new limbs. Preserve canonical jawless wooden face, crown with tree rings, moss distribution and exact character identity. Transform by opening bark, not making whole body explode. Eight distinct complete body key poses.

SHEET 05: HIT REACTION, BROKEN SUPPORT / VULNERABILITY, AND COMPLETE DEATH. Image 2 is canonical model/style reference only, do not copy its attack poses. Maintain same elevated camera and face DOWN toward viewer; same torso dimensions. TOP ROW (1) HIT RECOIL: right shoulder knocked backward, trunk twists slightly, one claw raised defensively, front root feet brace, heart flickers but no new wound or blood; (2) RECOVERY: weight settles back between four root feet, arms return to ready, same silhouette; (3) SUPPORT BREAK / STAGGER: rear root supports buckle and knees collapse asymmetrically, torso pitches sideways and front claws reach to arrest the fall, show a few broken root tips only, wood injury no gore; (4) VULNERABLE DOWNED POSE: torso lowered near ground, both arms limp to sides, bark plates open around exposed amber core, crown tilted forward, roots unable to support weight, clearly living and temporarily stunned. BOTTOM ROW chronological DEATH keys (5) heart fades to a tiny dim amber ember, eyes go dark, torso starts to sag and arms droop; (6) root legs fold fully under the SAME body, crown pitches forward, one claw rests on ground to side, core nearly dark; (7) stump topples onto its SIDE, show the actual same crown/tree rings rotating with the falling torso, heavy arms and roots spread inertly, remaining chest glow almost gone; (8) FINAL INERT REMAINS: recognizable split trunk lying horizontally on its side, both wooden arms and four root legs slack and partly folded, few attached bark fragments and small nearby splinters, core and eyes completely DARK. Do not replace body with unrelated pile of logs, do not dissolve, no explosion, no fire. Keep final corpse within the SAME cell at SAME physical scale; its fallen horizontal silhouette can be wider but may not cross cell boundaries. All limbs full in frame and minimum 20px transparent margin. No dirt ground patch.

correcao_vista_traseira: Precise image edit of this transparent 4-column by 2-row boss character pose sheet. CHANGE ONLY the THIRD character in the TOP ROW (the rear-view character at approximately 62.5% image width, 25% image height). Preserve all other SEVEN characters EXACTLY as drawn, preserve their positions, all transparent margins, pixel art rendering, canvas size, alpha transparency. That third character is currently an incorrect front torso without a glowing face. Completely REDRAW ONLY THAT THIRD CELL as the TRUE REAR VIEW of the same Cerne Partido boss: the monster faces AWAY, UP the screen. We see a broad continuous curved barrel-shaped BACK OF THE STUMP with overlapping rough vertical bark scales and a subtle central spine-like bark ridge, no pointed V-shaped front chest plate or opening, NO eyes, NO mouth, NO glowing amber core on the back. Show the REAR shoulder masses and backs of upper arms, elbow points facing the viewer, palms/claws turned away from us, and REAR root haunches and heels closest to camera with front root feet foreshortened beyond the trunk. Preserve four root legs rather than copy the front knees. Crown viewed from behind: show the tall jagged REAR rim nearest us, its jagged silhouette occluding part of the cut stump rings, front rim farther away. Same elevated top-down three-quarter camera as all other cells, same trunk width and physical scale, same 2 arms and 4 legs. The changed rear-view silhouette must be anatomically DIFFERENT from the front, not a front view with the eyes erased. It should unmistakably read as the BACK of the creature. Keep moss consistent with the reference. Absolutely no edits to the other seven poses. Transparent background, no text.
